name: Wisdom & the fear of the LORD
about: Proverbs and the wisdom that leads to Christ.

teachings.title: The love of money and the good fight of faith
teachings.summary: The love of money is the root of all evil, so the man of God flees it, is content with what God gives, and lays hold on eternal life and treasure in heaven.
teachings.text:
Paul continues, spinning off the warning about staying away from those who see earthly gain as proof of godliness, seeking after riches, we are given the adage "the love of money is the root of all evil." Storing up treasure on earth leads to temptations and snares, traps of our own making. Seeking after wealth while neglecting our stores in Heaven.

*O man of God, flee these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness.*

Be satisfied with what God blessed you with, even if it is subsistence, knowing that if you win souls, your riches in Heaven will be greater.

*Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.*

This is our calling, as those who have laid hold on eternal life; to live as though we believe it. That our hope isn't in vain, but on the promises of God, faithful and true.

The promise that as we live blamelessly, *unrebukable,* that when Christ returns for the Day of the Lord, everyone will get as they gave, and justice will be served. God's wrath upon those who have troubled us. Vengeance being His.

*Which in his times he shall shew, who is the blessed and only Potentate, the King of kings, and Lord of lords;*
*Who only hath immortality, dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto; whom no man hath seen, nor can see: to whom be honour and power everlasting. Amen.*

teachings.title: Make friends of the mammon of unrighteousness
teachings.summary: The unjust steward shows that worldly men use money wisely for the future, so Christians should use their wealth to bless others and lay up treasure in Heaven, for we cannot serve God and Mammon.
teachings.text:
We are in **Luke 16.** The chapter opens with Jesus speaking to His disciples, again impressing upon them the lessons He must as He makes His way to Jerusalem. Here, Jesus tells them parable of the unfaithful steward.

A dishonest steward is to be fired by his wealthy master for mismanagement of the lord's funds. Knowing he'd be out of a job, and not suited to labor or begging, decides to use his position to make deals with his master's debtors, forgiving their debts that they give him favor when he needs it. Buying their loyalty so when he's fired he can go to them for help. The master sees this scheme and, being corrupt himself can't help but be impressed by the servant's wisdom, his chutzpah and cunning.

And the lesson here for His disciples isn't that these men are good, or saved, but that sometimes the unsaved, in serving Mammon, understand better how the world works. How to win friends and influence people. *For the children of this world are in their generation wiser than the children of light.*

And so, Jesus says make friends with your wealth. Spend it to others benefit. Forgive them debts. Gain favor the way the unscrupulous servant has, that those you've helped may hear the Gospel, having had the trust gained, and welcome them in the Kingdom one day.

*He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.*

Your wealth does you no good here. Being stingy, miserly, storing up wealth in this world, is forsaking wealth in the next. In parallel passages the Bible says store up our wealth in heaven.

If a worldly unsaved man understands that he can use his position and wealth, the forgiveness of debts to gain favor with men against his future calamity,  how can a saved man not see it? There's more important things than money. Think of that future and how what you have can gain against our future in Heaven.

So, if we are greedy and niggardly, unwilling to give all charitably that we may do the work of Christ, how can God trust us with actual treasure? Incorruptible crowns? Authority in the Kingdom.

If we can't be just with unrighteous Mammon, how will we expect to be just with others souls?

*Ye cannot serve God and Mammon*.

teachings.title: Silver and gold cannot deliver them
teachings.summary: Covetousness is idolatry and riches cannot deliver in the day of wrath; you cannot serve God and Mammon.
teachings.text:
**Luke 21:20-22**
*And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh. Then let them which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto. For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.*

The wrath of God against the wicked is a promise, just as sure as salvation in Christ.

*They shall cast their silver in the streets, and their gold shall be removed: their silver and their gold shall not be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of the Lord: they shall not satisfy their souls, neither fill their bowels: because it is the stumblingblock of their iniquity.*

Covetousness is the sin of idolatry, the Bible says. And for the rich men, that store up treasure on earth, it is harder for them to enter into the kingdom of Heaven than for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle.

The stumbling block of their iniquity is their greed. Especially the Jews, who were and are respecters of persons in that regard.

Also from **Luke 21, 1-4**;
*And he looked up, and saw the rich men casting their gifts into the treasury. And he saw also a certain poor widow casting in thither two mites. And he said, Of a truth I say unto you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all: For all these have of their abundance cast in unto the offerings of God: but she of her penury hath cast in all the living that she had.*

The love of money is the root of all evil. You cannot serve God and Mammon.

This chapter also reminds me of the destruction of Babylon in **Revelation 18:9-19**;

 *And the kings of the earth, who have committed fornication and lived deliciously with her, shall bewail her, and lament for her, when they shall see the smoke of her burning, Standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come. And the merchants of the earth shall weep and mourn over her; for no man buyeth their merchandise any more: The merchandise of gold, and silver, and precious stones, and of pearls, and fine linen, and purple, and silk, and scarlet, and all thyine wood, and all manner vessels of ivory, and all manner vessels of most precious wood, and of brass, and iron, and marble, And cinnamon, and odours, and ointments, and frankincense, and wine, and oil, and fine flour, and wheat, and beasts, and sheep, and horses, and chariots, and slaves, and souls of men. And the fruits that thy soul lusted after are departed from thee, and all things which were dainty and goodly are departed from thee, and thou shalt find them no more at all. The merchants of these things, which were made rich by her, shall stand afar off for the fear of her torment, weeping and wailing, And saying, Alas, alas that great city, that was clothed in fine linen, and purple, and scarlet, and decked with gold, and precious stones, and pearls!  For in one hour so great riches is come to nought. And every shipmaster, and all the company in ships, and sailors, and as many as trade by sea, stood afar off, And cried when they saw the smoke of her burning, saying, What city is like unto this great city! And they cast dust on their heads, and cried, weeping and wailing, saying, Alas, alas that great city, wherein were made rich all that had ships in the sea by reason of her costliness! for in one hour is she made desolate.*

teachings.title: The portion of a wicked man
teachings.summary: Zophar spoke true wisdom at the wrong time: the wicked rich never have peace, their treasure perishes, so lay up treasure in heaven.
teachings.text:
Zophar the Naamathite joins in, again, and he says that all this back and forth with Job has triggered in him a need to interject, to speak with haste. He is going to proceed to give a recitation of wisdom, that is all undeniably true.

Everything in this monologue is accepted wisdom, and reflected in other teachings throughout the Bible. However, he neglected some of God's good advice;

**Ecclesiastes 5:2**
*Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.*

Despite the truth Zophar tells, the things he cannot wait to say, his timing and intent, as a reproach to Job and a counter to Job's chastisements of the froward trio, makes him a fool.

A real "*Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools*" moment.

But his words are wise in the right context. God is just to reward the hypocrite and those that work iniquity, even the rich man is punished in their unrighteousness, knowing that whatever they stored up in this life will perish. It will be spoiled and robbed, frittered away by their sons, returned to the soil and the people they took it from. And they all go down to the grave, returning to dust, the same as anyone else.

**Matthew 6:19-21**
*Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.*

The disquiet and fear that accompanies the gathering of wealth, the love of money and the evil that springs forth from its bitter root, that darkness in his secret places, not feeling quietness in his belly, will consume him in this life.

He will never know peace. Never be satisfied. Never feel sufficiency, and knowing the hands of the wicked are always at his throat.

The knowledge that his increase that fills his house, is fleeting. That all his goods will do nothing to protect him when God's wrath comes upon him. This is the punishment in this life for those who oppress the poor and take advantage of the righteous.

*This is the portion of a wicked man from God, and the heritage appointed unto him by God.*

teachings.title: Riches profit not in the day of wrath
teachings.summary: Riches cannot deliver from wrath but the imputed righteousness of Christ does, so the righteous give generously and lay up treasure in heaven rather than hoarding.
teachings.text:
The main themes presented in chapter 11 see the ways of the righteous compared to the transgressor, in matters of finance, fortune and benefit, and spiritual gain.

The delight of the Lord in our keeping of integrity and honesty in our dealings. Just measures, not cheating others, being upright in our dealings. God places an emphasis on our doing well for others when we could, in secret, selfishly gain at their expense. Doing good when no one is watching, while the froward man's perverse ways destroy them.

He warns that pride leads to shame and humility shows wisdom. How often have we seen pride lead to an almost immediate fall? In our own lives alone! Embarrassed and ashamed when we are puffed up. But walking in humility, we receive glory from God and others.

Solomon's wisdom shows a repeated contrast between the righteous being delivered and the wicked destroyed. That the generosity of the righteous builds up more wealth, the liberal soul made fat. Not only in this life, but the next.

*Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death,* reminds us that at the judgment, all the wealth in the world will do nothing to spare the wicked from wrath. Only the righteousness that is in Christ can. We are not appointed to wrath, by His mercy and imputed righteousness.

*The righteous is delivered out of trouble, and the wicked cometh in his stead.*

And so we should put the Kingdom first in our hearts;

Matthew 6:19-21
*Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.*

A warning that those that hoard and withhold being generous, or not selling their excess, will lead to poverty and worse in the day of judgement.

God loves a cheerful giver and sees fair and just enterprise as good. But hoarding and coveting, helps no one.

**Luke 12:16-21**
*And he spake a parable unto them, saying, The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plentifully: And he thought within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have no room where to bestow my fruits? And he said, This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I bestow all my fruits and my goods. And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry. But God said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided? So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.*

In the judgment, the hope of the wicked perishes, they shall not go unpunished. Their expectation is wrath. While the just and righteous shall be delivered.

The righteous, those who are fair, just, walking upright, speaking truth, walking in the way of the Lord, not only benefit themselves, but their community. Their city rejoices in them. They bring prosperity to their people. They are a blessing.

The wicked, however, curse their neighbors and overthrow their city. Being void of wisdom and unable to give counsel, despising their neighbors, bring destruction. They reveal secrets and are quick to mischief, and people suffer for their evil.

teachings.title: Rich yet nothing, poor yet rich
teachings.summary: Wealth itself is not sin, but true riches are being poor in spirit and content in Christ, and what matters is the spirit of a man and what he does with what he has.
teachings.text:
This lesson of wisdom and folly being the vision of long term rewards vs immediate gratification creates a seeming contradiction in **Proverbs 13:7**:

*There is that maketh himself rich, yet hath nothing: there is that maketh himself poor, yet hath great riches*.

How can a man make himself rich and have nothing, or poor and have everything? By faith in Christ Jesus.

**Matthew 5:3**
*Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.*

**Mark 8:36-37**
*For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?*

**Matthew 19:24** 
*And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.*

God is not opposed to earthly riches, to financial gain for His children. Proverbs is filled with calls to diligence and wisdom, that it be well with us and promises of substance and wealth if we do well.

Job and Abraham and Solomon were incredibly wealthy in their day. It isn't the wealth we gain but what we do with it. Being poor of spirit, that we humble ourselves before the Lord. Being filled with gratitude and delayed satisfaction, liberal and generous with what we have, putting other's profit above our own.

Being financially poor is not always a sign of wickedness. But the ways of the wicked lead to poverty and shame. The poor heareth not rebuke. But the poor man may be wise and rich in Christ. The rich man may be so by wisdom, but it is harder for one with riches to do what's right.

It isn't the wealth but the spirit of a man. It isn't their gain but what they do with it. It isn't the riches but where your treasure is. This is not a contradiction, but discernment and Wisdom. Wealth isn't the point, but the willingness to follow the word of God, and to be satisfied with what He provides.

**Philippians 4:11-13**
*Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content. I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.* Amen!

teachings.title: Low time preference is a sign of wisdom
teachings.summary: The wise son receives instruction and reproof, and his diligence and willingness to delay gratification for a later harvest is wisdom, while the fool's haste and greed destroy him.
teachings.text:
Now the wise son, who takes instruction and reproof, who learns from the word and the scourging, his end is sweet. A good father who loves him enough to instruct and chasten. A God who does the same. This results in prudence and discretion, diligence in labors, rejecting the way of the sluggards. Hatred of lying, keeping in the upright way, watching their tongue, what proceeds from their lips.

**Matthew 15:11, 17-20**
*Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man...Do not ye yet understand, that whatsoever entereth in at the mouth goeth into the belly, and is cast out into the draught? But those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man. For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies: These are the things which defile a man: but to eat with unwashen hands defileth not a man.*

The light of the righteous man does shine and those that receive it rejoice, the wisdom of good counsel, rewards all who harken to it.

*Whoso despiseth the word shall be destroyed: but he that feareth the commandment shall be rewarded.* This gospel theme continues to be hammered in Proverbs, and the spiritual application of this wisdom is undeniable, but the practical meaning cannot be ignored. God tells us over and over of the reward of obedience to His commandments. The long life, the blessings and the abundance of wealth all come to those who are wise and fear the Lord, and His commands. His promises are sure:

*The law of the wise is a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death.*

This good understanding brings favor. God's grace, making our way easier. The sinners life is hard.

Diligence is rewarded, but this wise trait is often coupled with the wisdom of delaying gratification. Putting off their desires, knowing a greater reward awaits. Knowing to scatter the seed, in anticipation of a later harvest. Building up stores to the winter, but being generous with what you have, not being too short sighted to miss how that benefits you in the long run. How to wait patiently on the Lord.

*The desire accomplished is sweet to the soul.*..*Hope deferred maketh the heart sick: but when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life.* Hard work pays off. Quick riches fade but he that gathers by labor gains increase.

Low time preference is the behavioral tendency to delay immediate gratification in favor of future, long-term rewards. It reflects a patient, disciplined, and forward-thinking mindset that values hard work, prudence, acquiring knowledge and understanding, and it is a sign of wisdom.

The foolish are sluggards, they have high time preference and are easily tempted into sin. They covet, they seek mischief and violence, they gain their wealth by vanity, only to loose it. When they do store up against the future, they allow their greed to keep them from using it wisely, and it corrupts and rots, it's turned over to the just to recompense for evil, and is stolen or lost - *destroyed for want of judgement.*

teachings.title: Boast not thyself of tomorrow
teachings.summary: Tomorrow is not promised, which makes today the day of salvation, so we should not boast or procrastinate nor be paralyzed by worry, but be prudent and diligent now.
teachings.text:
The record of Solomon's wisdom, as recorded by King Hezekiah's scribes, continues in **Proverbs 27**.

The litany of sayings found here offers some new insights, retelling of others and repetition of yet more, all for our edification.

The chapter begins with the understanding that we should not assume what the future brings. We are prisoners of the moment, and our breath is in God's hands. Tomorrow isn't promised.

We primarily use this Biblical understanding to stress the urgency of the gospel when preaching to the lost. That getting your account settled on the way cannot wait. Because, as the Bible says in **2 Corinthians 6:2** ...*I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.*

If you haven't trusted on Christ as your only means of salvation, given by the grace of the Father, now is the time.

If you have received that precious gift, get to work doing the will of God and winning souls. **Romans 13:11** ..*.now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed*

But even in general terms, boasting about what you will do tomorrow is an empty promise when you don't know what lies in store.

**James 4:14-15**
*Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away. For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.*

God willing, it shall come to pass, but better to deal with today, redeem the time and accomplish what may be done now, than seek glory for what you've yet to do. And even then, boast not at all;

*Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips.*

It is in the nature of finite man to boast on the morrow while we procrastinate difficult things. To justify our not doing anything now, because of how wonderful our plans are for then. Getting lazy. Saying "If it's God's will" as an excuse.

But what then? Should we not plan for the things that may come? To just wait on the Lord for all things? Not at all. Verse 12;

*A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself; but the simple pass on, and are punished.*

Some, rather than foolishly passing on, or boasting on what they may do, get so caught up in worry for tomorrow that they are paralyzed today. Jesus teaches us to avoid that as well;

**Matthew 6:34**
*Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.*

We should recognize that the future exists, and the evil thereof, and plan accordingly. Being diligent in the works of today, is being prudent for tomorrow.

*Whoso keepeth the fig tree shall eat the fruit thereof: so he that waiteth on his master shall be honoured.*

This is the correct balance, to see the future as an opportunity that's built in the work of the present, guarding against evil, while knowing the harvest will come. The reward is waiting. The honor and glory will come. Whether serving God and the spiritual works as a laborer for Christ, or just in your daily life in taking care of those things God has put before us.

Achieve balance, seek Him first, be prudent and plan, without worry, don't out off till tomorrow what can be done today. Do not seek your own glory and honor, or boast about what you plan to do, but work diligently knowing you will earn the praise of others, even God, Amen.

teachings.title: Know the state of thy flocks
teachings.summary: Riches do not last, so diligently manage what God provides and, how much more, tend the flocks He has given us to serve, from a child to a church.
teachings.text:
*Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle, yet will not his foolishness depart from him.*

This saying carries another reminder that fools are locked in to their foolishness, that they are wise in their own conceit and even stripes won't make them listen. Not even grinding them in a mortar and pestle could remove their foolishness.

Finally, as in earlier parts of the chapter, is the lesson in the diligence of now, the favoring of low time preference and having a long view.

Tend your flocks. Look well to thy herds. Manage the resources and wealth you have, and don't be wasteful or careless. Riches are not forever. The crown does not endure to every generation. These things can be squandered and lost by poor management, slothfulness and foolishness.

God provides the tender grass and herbs of the mountain. The food for your flock. The means of your substance. The ability to make a living depends on His grace and generosity, and our diligence.

Keeping this in mind, He promises that we shall have what is sufficient to care for our family.

If we take care of our worldly wealth, and manage and work it, taking advantage of all the Lord provides, how much more the treasure we store up in Heaven?

The Lord provides us His word to feed the flock, as the grass and herb. We all have opportunities to serve Him and reach the lost, to tend to the flocks He has given us. It may a mother over her child. It may be as a teacher to young men. It may be as a Pastor over a church. But our diligence to know the state of them, and look well over our herd, will benefit ourselves and our family in the long run.

teachings.title: He that hasteth to be rich
teachings.summary: Lack of understanding breeds covetousness, which prosperity-gospel con men and false teachers exploit, while the faithful man who works diligently abounds in blessings.
teachings.text:
Continuing the series on Proverbs chapter 28; *The prince that wanteth understanding is also a great oppressor: but he that hateth covetousness shall prolong his days*.

This saying ties together two seemingly disparate concepts, but as advice to a young prince of the kingdom, they tie together. Lack of understanding leads to covetousness. Not having knowledge and the wisdom to execute it, leads to a desire for things. As we've already discussed, regarding the rich young man and Jesus, want for understanding and desire for "things" go hand in hand. Longing for riches, seeking what's not yours, fills the hole that's left.

Vs 17 warns to let the bloody man go to where his violence shall take him. To his own violent end.

Vs 18-28 are another set of contrasting sayings, between the good man and wicked, but focusing on a particular type of behavior that is driven by seeking gain without the work it takes to earn it. And warnings against being corrupt enough to be taken in by vain men.

Those who walk upright, honest in their dealings shall be saved. Not necessarily in the gospel sense, although that may apply, but in the "sudden destruction" that comes upon the wicked. The man perverse in his ways will see their life fall apart quickly. A corrupt and crooked politician, suddenly exposed as a degenerate and a whoremonger, for example. It is as inevitable as the bloody man's race to the pit.

The prudent man, who tilleth his land, who tends to the fields now that they may harvest later, will have plenty. But those that follow after vain persons shall have poverty.

The vain hope in flatterers, seducers and false teachers, perverse political leaders, will take those that follow them, by covetousness and sloth, itchy ears and lusts. But there is no profit in the energy expended on vain pursuit.

*A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent.*..*To have respect if persons is not good: for for a piece of bread that man will transgress...He that hastens to be rich hath an evil eye, and consdereth not that poverty shall come upon him.*

The theme of covetousness and following after vain persons really hits hard in v20-22. The faithful man will abound with blessings, but those looking to get rich quick choose to corrupt themselves in their greed.

The "Prosperity Gospel" scam artists take as much advantage of this tendency in man as the street corner swindler. The old secular saying, "you can't con an honest man" is simply resting this biblical truth.

Having respect of persons, favoring one over others because of their wealth, their position, their power, is wrong, not only because it leads to treating the poor and powerless as less than yourself, but instills a form of covetousness in your heart that makes it easier for these false teachers, crept in unawares, to make merchandise of you.

This tendency towards greedy covetousness and seeking to gain favor with those you favor for appearance and empty promises, will lead you to sell out for a piece of bread. For a small fraction of what you could have earned honestly with prudent diligence.

He that hasteneth to be rich, is being guided by their evil eye, not by the ways of the Lord.

**1 John 2:16**
*For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.*

This can strike anyone, at any age or station. Presidents and kings can be taken out by the same lusts peddled by vain men, as the poorest man.

They delude themselves that their end won't be poverty, but as we've seen, the perverse in his ways shall fall all at once. And great is that fall.

Better to be the upright man who rebukes those being taken in by the flattering tongue of a con man. Better to till your field for a future harvest. Better to do the work of the Lord for rewards in Heaven.

teachings.title: Rich toward God, not laying up treasure
teachings.summary: Hoarded riches are vanity because a man takes nothing with him, as the rich fool shows, so the good portion is to enjoy God's gift and be rich toward God.
teachings.text:
Coming back around to his main theme, the vanity and vexation of spirit that this life and the cares of the world that beset us all, Solomon addresses those that horde wealth. Who greedily gathers increase to themselves.

He says the riches they keep are to their own hurt. That their heir is born without, and will die as all men, without. You can't take it with you. Even in an inheritance, is vanity.

It is a sore evil, the preacher says, that the profit of excessive gain is like the wind. The man labors for more and more, yet will have nothing in death.

Jesus teaches on this, as well.

**Luke 12:16-21**
*And he spake a parable unto them, saying, The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plentifully: And he thought within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have no room where to bestow my fruits? And he said, This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I bestow all my fruits and my goods. And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry. But God said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided? So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.*

It is vanity.

And so, Solomon brings it back around to the one good thing he has found under the Sun; the blessing of God that a man may enjoy the good of his labor in this life. That the portion of the rich man, as it is for the poor, is to take and rejoice in the fruit of their works. That this is a gift from God.

teachings.title: The curse of Adam behind the vanity of labour
teachings.summary: The endless labour, unfilled appetite and death that make life vain are the direct result of Adam's sin and the curse on the ground.
teachings.text:
**Ecclesiastes 6** continues the Preacher's lament on the vanity of wealth and increase in a fleeting human life, but that the gift of God is the good of enjoying the fruits of that labor, in this life.

The evil Solomon sees all too often is this; that for all a man gains, ultimately it goes to others. And so, if God gifts a man riches, wealth and honor, having everything he ever could want, what good is it if that same man was not given by the Lord the ability to enjoy it?

Solomon reasons, *If a man beget an hundred children, and live many years, so that the days of his years be many, and his soul be not filled with good, and also that he have no burial; I say, that an untimely birth is better than he.*

He says that if a man were not blessed to enjoy the good life that his efforts earned, living long with many children, if he die alone and in darkness, without even a proper burial despite his 100 children, he is worse off than a stillborn child.

That the soul that never saw the sun, nor known anything of this world is better off than to have the vanity of travails and not be able to enjoy what comes of it.

*All the labour of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.* We are never satisfied, but must work to feed ourselves.

Writing to the Thessalonians, Paul commands *that if any would not work, neither should he eat.* This is not only a maxim of truth, warning against idleness and sluggards taking advantage of the more enterprising in the church, but hunger is a reminder of the curse upon man that came from Adam's fall.

**Genesis 3:17-19** 
*And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field; In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.*

The vanity of life, the endless labor and the vexation of spirit, knowing that ultimately, other than the portion we are given to enjoy by God, is gone when we return to dust, is a direct result of sin.

Knowing that the endless cycle of work and the certainty of death is vain, yet necessary, what is the point without the blessings of God, that we may at least eat and drink and enjoy what we earn?

So he asks rhetorically, what advantage does the wise have over the fool? Or the poor that walks in the Lord's paths? It is that reward and blessing that comes from God for doing well.

Better to keep in mind that which is set before you, the sight of the eyes, to do what you can and let God bring the increase, than to give in to covetousness and greed, the wandering of desire. Because that need to seek ever more, rather than being grateful for what you have, is vanity and vexation of spirit.

teachings.title: Say not the former days were better
teachings.summary: Longing for better former days is a snare; there is no political solution to a spiritual problem, so we redeem the present time and give our children the wisdom of God.
teachings.text:
*Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad; and a gift destroyeth the heart.*

This aside, noting that under stress and oppression a wise man may be driven to madness and in wrath, commit sin, or by bribery, brought to do wrong, sets up a subtle transition.

Testing his thesis, the idea that the end is better than the beginning, Solomon notes the human limits of wisdom and righteousness. Things which may make it appear that all things under the Sun grow progressively worse.

The proverb of v9-10 warns against the tendency to see things this way; *Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.* *Say not thou, What is the cause that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not enquire wisely concerning this.*

This tendency, especially among the righteous who walk in the ways of God as much as lies within them, is a snare. It leads to sin that we are all guilty of at times.

"Make America Great, Again," and calls to RETVRN! and other appeals to the "better days" of the past prey upon the inclination to see the former days as better, especially given the evil we see all around us. For we all feel like Lot at times.

**2 Peter 2:7-8**
*And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)*

But coveting the past takes us away from doing what we are supposed to in the present.

There is no political solution to a spiritual problem. Revival is a continuous process. The need for revival is never greater than now. No matter when "now" is.

To enquirer wisely, it is better to ask God to straighten that which He has made crooked. To seek God to make the hardships given to teach us wisdom worthwhile. Rather than curse that things are the way they are, which is vanity.

If we seek His wisdom from adversity, we gain. We gain understanding and, by our diligence in tribulation, wealth. And both serve as an inheritance to our children, a defense, Solomon writes. It is profitable to our future to redeem the time in the present, rather than getting angry about a past we cannot change.

The excellency of knowledge is the wisdom that giveth life. This is what we should consider. Giving to our children the understanding of God.

Solomon reiterates the understanding that we should rejoice in the good days, for the prosperity God grants, while also considering that God gives adversity as well, and for our own good. He sets the two against each other, that we find nothing after Him.

teachings.title: Your labour is not in vain in the Lord
teachings.summary: Works done for the Lord are never in vain, and the good things of this life, a wife, food and drink, are gifts of God's grace to be enjoyed.
teachings.text:
Solomon's preaching on the vanity of life leads us inevitably to consider the works done for the Lord, which are never in vain.

**1 Corinthians 15:58**
 *Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.*

We have to understand that the preacher is appealing to the life of man, which is short and brutal. But spiritually, those that are wise fear the Lord. And those works that we do have lasting impact. And the rewards we receive, they are blessings from God.

We only know love because He so loved us.

**1 John 4:7-8**
*Beloved, let us love one another: for love is of God; and every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God.He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.*

We know a wife is a gift from God. We know the fruit of our labors in being able to enjoy it comes from Him. We know the sweet things of life, to eat, drink and be merry, is of God.

All good things are of God. And it's okay to enjoy those things. They are a gift. They are examples of His grace.

*Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun. Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.*

teachings.title: The vanity of riches before death
teachings.summary: Wise and fool, rich and poor all die, riches cannot ransom a soul, and only the fear of the Lord and redemption through Christ give hope in the day of wrath.
teachings.text:
Psalm 49 is a meditation on the futility of life, in the building of of riches, honor and name, when death awaits everyone, rich or poor, wise or fool.

This reflection on life's vanities ties to Solomon's writings in **Ecclesiastes**, from the call to harken to the preacher to the vanity of life and the only remedy, fearing the Lord and receiving His blessing.

**Ecclesiastes 2:16**
*For there is no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; seeing that which now is in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And how dieth the wise man? as the fool.*

This echoes the same sentiment found in verse 10;

*For he seeth that wise men die, likewise the fool and the brutish person perish, and leave their wealth to others.*

**Ecclesiastes 5:15**
*As he came forth of his mother's womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.*

Solomon learned at the feet of his father, and after careful study of all the things his wealth and power availed him of, with the wisdom above other men, granted by God's grace, he would come to the same conclusions David sang of.

The call to incline your ear to hear wisdom, to listen to the dark sayings and parables. To seek understanding is a major theme of Solomon's **Proverbs**;

**Proverbs 4:7**
*Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.*

David teaches us the same lessons in Psalms. The wisdom of God is most valuable, because in that knowledge we may find eternal life.

David expresses confidence in his salvation. He is not afraid when the time comes to be given the wages of his sin, the iniquity of his heels, the death that awaits us all, the consequences of our own making.

Why should we fear in the days of evil, that comes our own making? He knows his redemption is a gift of God. But the man trusting his riches has no hope at all in that day. They cannot redeem themselves or their brothers, and cannot pay the ransom due God for their sins.

Again, this idea that man's riches are worthless in the judgment, that they do nothing for the dead, is repeated by Solomon;

**Proverbs 11:4**
*Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.*

**Proverbs 27:24**
*For riches are not for ever: and doth the crown endure to every generation?*

Their way is folly. The wise man dies like the fool, like the brute, and all their wealth is left for others. But the precious redemption of the soul, that one lives forever and shall not see corruption, that is of God, through faith in the Lord Christ Jesus.

**1 Timothy 2:5–6**
*For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus; Who gave himself a ransom for all, to be testified in due time.*

David laments the fact that worldly prosperity deceives the wealthy, their own riches fooling them into a false sense of security. This is the larger context of the preaching of Christ;

**Matthew 19:23–26**
*Then said Jesus unto his disciples, Verily I say unto you, That a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven. And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God. When his disciples heard it, they were exceedingly amazed, saying, Who then can be saved? But Jesus beheld them, and said unto them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.*

The only hope of man, rich or poor, is God. Only in Him is salvation possible.

**Proverbs 15:16**
*Better is little with the fear of the Lord than great treasure and trouble therewith.*

The blessings of this life are not a hope for the next. The praise of men is vanity before the Throne of an almighty and holy God.

Agur's  prayer in **Proverbs** directly addresses this wisdom;

**Proverbs 30:8-9**
*Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.*

teachings.title: The preaching of the cross is foolishness to them that perish
teachings.summary: Paul rebukes divisions over who baptized whom and teaches that the gospel looks foolish to those seeking signs or human reasoning, while God makes our weakness and meekness His strength.
teachings.text:
After his greeting and the establishment or, re-establishment of the shared belief that unites those in Corinth, Paul gets to the heart of the matter in that he has heard reports of division in the church. Those who had been saved by Paul, or Apollos or Peter, and even those who had been saved during the ministry of Jesus Christ, are beginning to form schisms and divisions.

Paul is admonishing this, and points out that the baptism and who did it is incidental to the saving faith in Christ Jesus, in whose name they were baptized all. We see this a lot today, people treating what should be a unifying faith as a scene, and bickering about personalities within the scene. This is a real problem and, the denominational splits that we see in the church later all stem from it. Especially the schism that gives birth to the Roman Catholic Church 300 years later, and all of the devastation to Christianity that spun out of it.

Paul reminds them that the baptism isn't what they're there for, but to preach the gospel. Here Paul makes several doctrinal statements regarding the preaching of the Gospel that are both sublime truth, and yet obvious to those of us who are saved upon hearing it.

That the preaching of the Cross appears to be foolish to those who are either seeking after a sign from God, or to be reasoned with into faith. As Jesus said the only sign the Jews would receive was that of Jonas, of his being in the belly of the Earth for three days and three nights to be risen again. And for the greeks, who sought a reason above all, giving them faith which is the evidence of things unseen, in lieu of logic, appears to be foolishness.

We all know people today who are constantly looking for supernatural signs from God before they can commit to believing, or physical evidence of the truth of the Bible from secular sources. Or who seek to impose their own logic on matters that are spiritual. And who stuff at the simplicity of the Gospel as it's presented, despite our knowledge of the power of God that is within it.

Similar to the Epistle of James that we read over the weekend, Paul notes that the proud and wealthy, the powerful etc, are less likely to receive the Gospel because God uses our weaknesses to become our strength. Our humility and meekness becomes power in the hands of a believing Son of God. And what many see as foolishness, or weakness and passivity, or supposed slave mentality, is actually the wisdom of God expressed through our understanding, patience, long suffering, and the love that we show to all.

A lot of people grapple with this even saved Christians. They seek their own vengeance, they carry the wrath that belongs to God, they grow impatient with His perfect timing. For those who are not saved by faith, these things are a snare and a stumbling block, their pride being caught in those traps.

teachings.title: The Wisdom of God Against the Vexation of the World
teachings.summary: The wisdom of this world brings despair, but the foolishness of the gospel gives rest, wisdom and joy to all who come to Christ.
teachings.text:
The despondency of the natural man is manifest in how we react to the wisdom of this world. To the toil and drudgery that is a life without meaning. The same folly that our fathers endured and that our children will face. The wickedness and sin throughout the world. Evil called good and good, evil. The weakness of others and the burdens they become on our shoulders. A yoke that leads to bitterness, resentment, wrath, covetousness and a host of other sins and the vices that we take up to fill the time and dull the pain. Even a "good man" has their patience stretched thin and feels the despair more acutely it seems.

But then there's the wisdom of God, which makes the weak strong and brings forth the truth of the things the world hates to bring to nought that which they love.

And the foolishness of the Gospel is the power unto salvation. That God became man, dwelled among us, sinless, to do the will of God unto death that we who deserve Hell are made righteous in His blood. And the resurrection of Christ giving us the hope of our faith, that we have eternal life through the grace and mercy of God the Father.

And by that faith, we are given wisdom and knowledge and strength. The power of sanctification and redemption in the day of judgment that all men are appointed to.

And so, we rejoice. We rejoice in tribulation knowing we have triumphed. We give glory to God in suffering and in blessings. We patiently wait for His return, while being a light to those still in darkness.

If you're not 100% certain, today, right now, that if you died today you would go to Heaven. If you're scared and alone and feel hopeless. If you're carrying guilt and trauma and regrets that are tearing you up inside. If you're seeking answers and wisdom, but only finding despair and vexation. If you're struggling to find an identity, a place in a world that makes no sense to you at times. If you have been laboring to be righteous, to cleanse your sins by your own works, and frustrated with how fruitless it is to obtain righteousness on your own, please consider this presentation of the Bible way to Heaven. You don't have to carry the burden. Jesus already has done it for you.

*Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.*

teachings.title: True things used to make false points
teachings.summary: Eliphaz's vision uses true doctrine about God's holiness and judgment to make a false point, showing great lies are built on misapplied truths.
teachings.text:
Eliphaz continues, letting us know of a vision that he had just before sleep, of a spirit he thinks he glimpsed and a voice he heard, that asked:

*Shall mortal man be more just than God? shall a man be more pure than his maker? Behold, he put no trust in his servants; and his angels he charged with folly: How much less in them that dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, which are crushed before the moth?*

His private interpretation, his own inner musings that he paints as a spiritual vision, posits that since man is obviously not as holy as God, and if even the Angels were punished for their rebellion, how much more man is under judgment for our wickedness, men, whose life is but a vapor and to dust we return, crushed as easily as the moth.

And it is true that God reserved punishment for the angels *which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day..*

**2 Peter 2:4**
*For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment*.

And in **Hebrews 2:6-7** (paraphrasing **Psalm 8:5**) *What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man that thou visitest him? Thou madest him a little lower than the angels...*

Again, Eliphaz uses true things to make false points.

And because it is true that God punishes the wicked, that he spared not the angels that kept not their estate but sinned, and that all men die, and their bodies decay and their excellency goes away. And it happens to the wise and those without wisdom alike.

**Ecclesiastes 9:2**
*All things come alike to all: there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth, and to him that sacrificeth not: as is the good, so is the sinner; and he that sweareth, as he that feareth an oath.*

Many times the greatest lies are based on a misrepresentation or misapplication of the greatest truths.

teachings.title: Jesus the vein of wisdom
teachings.summary: Wisdom is worth more than gold or rubies, begins with the fear of the Lord, and all its treasures are hid in Christ.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 9:10**
*The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.*

Job describes the relative ease of finding precious stones, silver, gold, iron and brass, compared to the wisdom of God.

**Proverbs 8:11**
*For wisdom is better than rubies; and all the things that may be desired are not to be compared to it.*

**Colossians 2:2-3**
*That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love, and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the acknowledgement of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ; In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.*

In Christ is all God's wisdom and knowledge. Other creatures and creation is nothing compared to Him. Only in Him is understanding. Jesus is the vein of wisdom, through the fear of God.

teachings.title: We have the mind of Christ
teachings.summary: 1 Corinthians 2:14 was written to carnal believers at Corinth, so walking in the flesh cuts a saved man off from the wisdom of God, which is found in the fear of the Lord and departing from evil.
teachings.text:
**1 Corinthians 2:7-16**
*But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom, which God ordained before the world unto our glory: Which none of the princes of this world knew: for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory. But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him. But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God. For what man knoweth the things of a man, save the spirit of man which is in him? even so the things of God knoweth no man, but the Spirit of God. Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God; that we might know the things that are freely given to us of God. Which things also we speak, not in the words which man's wisdom teacheth, but which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual. But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned. But he that is spiritual judgeth all things, yet he himself is judged of no man. For who hath known the mind of the Lord, that he may instruct him? but we have the mind of Christ.*

What an awesome thing. To have the mind of Christ. But, our flesh is at enmity with the spirit, and so when we walk in the canal, we have less access to the wisdom of God.

We often use **1 Corinthians 2:14** to say that unbelievers cannot understand scripture, but Paul is writing to the church at Corinth to tell them to stop being carnal. They're arguing over personalities of men, who is of Paul and who is of Apollos, and so they are natural men, and shutting themselves off from that font of wisdom in Jesus Christ. The spiritual things of God.

*That your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God. Howbeit we speak wisdom among them that are perfect: yet not the wisdom of this world, nor of the princes of this world, that come to nough*

Job understands that to even begin to grasp the unsearchable richness of the God, that fear of the Lord and departing from evil is where understanding is found.

teachings.title: The fear of the Lord the beginning of knowledge
teachings.summary: Proverbs was given to make men wise through the fear of the Lord, and parents are commanded to teach these truths to their children, the greatest inheritance they can leave.
teachings.text:
The book of Proverbs is given to man, a gift of God with a very specific purpose.

*To know wisdom and instruction; to perceive the words of understanding; To receive the instruction of wisdom, justice, and judgment, and equity; To give subtilty to the simple, to the young man knowledge and discretion.*

Much of the book of wisdom is by Solomon, who God gave an abundance of wisdom and knowledge and understanding, who as King displayed this wisdom in ruling, making Israel great again. But in his personal life, not so much.

It is astounding how we, as men, can hear God's word, know His word, study it, hear it preached, and yet still lean on our own understanding, rather than in all our ways acknowledging Him that He may direct our paths.

*A wise man will hear, and will increase learning; and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels: To understand a proverb, and the interpretation; the words of the wise, and their dark sayings.The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.*

God's word should lead us to fear Him. To respect His holiness, power, mercy and justice. His wrath and His judgments. This is what makes a man wise, our fearful respect for the Lord, and being doers of the word, increases our knowledge and faith.

Solomon writes, *My son, hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother,* these truths are from God, and it is every parent's responsibility to teach them to our children, that they be an ornament of grace upon their head, and chains about their necks. It is the greatest inheritance we can give our children. It is also a command: Raising them in the fear and knowledge of God, to bring *them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.*

teachings.title: The paths of judgment and the way
teachings.summary: The paths of Proverbs are the way, the doctrines of Christ, and discretion keeps us on them and delivers us from the evil man and the strange woman whose paths lead to death.
teachings.text:
Continuing **Proverbs 2** we see the the Lord giveth wisdom, and the paths of judgment preserves the way of His saints. The paths analogy is used throughout Proverbs, and the way, is the doctrines of Christ. Early Christians were said to be followers of the way. We hear about keeping the old paths. God's word is a light unto out feet, and He directs our paths when we acknowledge Him.

This understanding is very much the beginning of wisdom. Knowing where you've been and where you're going, seeing down the road. Knowing there's an end. Knowing the journey can lead you from the straight path, to the left or right. It is this understanding that gives us our first discernment, to see "If I continue this way, danger" knowing there are consequences "down the road."

We see God's ways are not our own, but in His knowledge we get righteous judgement, to see every good path. The way.

And that discretion preserves us, keeping us safe. Delivering us from the evil man, the froward who walk in paths of darkness. Or laying in wait on uncertain, or crooked ways.

This discretion delivers us from the strange woman, the counterpoint of Wisdom. The strange woman forsakes the good paths, the ways of her youth, the covenant of God.

Her paths lead to death. Wisdom's, to life.

We are called to learn God's ways to avoid that snare. To walk the way of good men. To keep the paths or righteousness. And the promise of God is that, by keeping to Wisdom and her paths, we will be upright and true. His saints, sanctified in His Son. That we will dwell in the land.

But the curse of those who don't keep the way, who choose the strange woman, and her paths of death; being cut off from the earth, and rooted our of it.

**Jude 1:12** *These are spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you, feeding themselves without fear: clouds they are without water, carried about of winds; trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots*...

Cast into the blackness of darkness forever.

teachings.title: Trust in the Lord, lean not on thine own understanding
teachings.summary: Proverbs 3:5-6 is the key verse of the book: acknowledge God first and keep His old paths, and honour Him with your substance out of gratitude, not as a prosperity gospel.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Proverbs 3**, building on the understanding given already; that fear of God brings knowledge, His word brings discernment, and the Wisdom of God is the fruit of following His ways over our own.

Following the way, walking His paths, being doers of the word and not hearers only, is Wisdom. But following other paths is like going in unto a strange woman, whose ways lead to death.

But what are the advantages of knowing and keeping God's ways? Obeying His commandments?

*For length of days, and long life, and peace, they shall add to thee*.

God's commandments have promises. And it just makes sense that since the wages of sin is death, righteousness is life.

Mercy and truth are the most precious of God's commandments. His mercy towards us shows the value of mercy to others. Truth guides us to judge righteous judgment.

Jews today literally bind the words of the law to their arms, and in boxes on their forehead. They take the promise of finding favor of God and men for "binding" literally, and *omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith*.

*Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.*

This is the key verse of Proverbs. The foundational understanding. Remember it, sing it, say it. And in everything acknowledge God first.

Be not wise in your own eyes, don't lean on your understanding. Don't think to blaze your own trails and beat down your own paths. There is nothing new under the Sun and God's ways are the best ways. The old paths, tried and true.

And following them brings health.

And honoring the Lord by giving of your substance, your riches, the first portion of your increase, will bring prosperity.

Note this isn't a prosperity gospel, but show that gratitude for the blessings He provides, and acknowledging Him first, will see our blessing compound. He rewards gratitude and hates murmuring.

teachings.title: The root of the righteous shall not be moved
teachings.summary: Proverbs carries a consistent gospel message: a man is made good by faith that comes by the word, and the root of righteousness is Christ, not Israel as dispensationalists claim nor Peter as Catholics claim.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 12** opens with another reminder that loving instruction and knowledge is precious, and the way of righteousness, while hating correction and wisdom is brutish and wicked.

And verse two reiterates that a good man - the just, wise, fearful of God who seeks after knowledge and walks in His ways, obtains favor from the Lord, but the wicked are condemned.

**Proverbs 9:10**
*The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding*.

**Hebrews 11:6**
*But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.*

**Romans 10:17**
*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*

**Romans 5:1-2**
*Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ: By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God.*

**Ephesians 2:8**
*For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God*...

We see how a man is made good, by the fear of God and hearing of His word, by faith seeking Him and truth, and by faith we have access to His grace, we obtain the favor of the Lord, receiving His gift of salvation.

The consistent gospel message of Proverbs cannot be overlooked.

Wickedness cannot establish a man, but the root of Righteousness, that is Christ Jesus, shall not be moved. He is the "root of Jesse" and a "branch of righteousness" (**Isaiah 11, Jeremiah 23:5-6**), established as the foundational righteousness for all believers. Through faith, believers are grafted into this root, allowing them to bear the fruit of righteousness, by the precious seed of His word.

Romans 11:16-18 
*For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches. And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert grafted in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; Boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee.*

Dispensationalists will claim the root is Israel, but it has always been Christ. Just as Catholics will claim Peter, "a stone," is the rock, which actually is the profession that Jesus is Christ. Because no other foundation can be laid;

**1 Corinthians 3:11**
*For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.*

All wisdom leads to Christ.

**Matthew 7:24-25** 
*Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.*

teachings.title: A way which seemeth right unto a man
teachings.summary: Because the heart is deceitful, the way that seems right to man ends in death, and the backslider is filled with his own ways, so we must keep our heart sound.
teachings.text:
Again, in verse 11 we see the wise builder's tabernacle flourishes when the wicked's will be overthrown. Not the structure, tent of building but the nature of the home. The family.

*There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.* God's ways are not our ways. Our heart is deceitful and wicked. The things we think are right or the things of God we see as counterintuitive, often lacks perspective. Longview. Or are based on lies we tell ourselves to justify our sin. Prideful and graceless. Even the things we may laugh at, the Bible says, our heart remains sorrowful. Even in mirth is heaviness. Who can know man's heart?

And so, *The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways: and a good man shall be satisfied from himself.* When we fall into sin, leaving the good path of the Lord, backsliding from whatever progress we have made, not walking in the Spirit but our own desires, we are filled with our own judgement.

*A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones.*

We should be mindful of our heart, to keep it sound. To limit what we give into when we heed it. To know the spirit where what we desire comes from.

teachings.title: The Lord hath made all things for himself
teachings.summary: God judges the spirit behind men's deeds and uses even the wicked, like Assyria, for His purposes, so we should commit our works to Him and walk in the fear of the Lord, which brings wisdom and makes even our enemies be at peace with us.
teachings.text:
Following the opening verse, we get a quick succession of proverbs that highlight the way of the Lord, and insight to His understanding.

The Lord judges the ways of a man by the spirit behind what we do. Men may justify every deed and word, but it is the intent and heart behind them that God cares about. A man can do good for bad reasons, he can do evil with good intentions. We do things in ignorance, we do things willfully, and so God judges righteous judgement, as only He can.

And so, to ensure we are walking in His ways, we are encouraged to commit our works to the Lord and our thoughts will be established. The spirit behind our deeds will be His, rather than our vain rationalizations.

The Lord has made all creation, everything that is, is His. Even the wicked who do evil serve a purpose for the Lord. Consider Assyria;

**Isaiah 10:1-6**
*Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees, and that write grievousness which they have prescribed; To turn aside the needy from judgment, and to take away the right from the poor of my people, that widows may be their prey, and that they may rob the fatherless! And what will ye do in the day of visitation, and in the desolation which shall come from far? to whom will ye flee for help? and where will ye leave your glory? Without me they shall bow down under the prisoners, and they shall fall under the slain. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still. O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger, and the staff in their hand is mine indignation. I will send him against an hypocritical nation, and against the people of my wrath will I give him a charge, to take the spoil, and to take the prey, and to tread them down like the mire of the streets.*

The destruction of the northern kingdom of Israel by the heathen empire was done by the wicked. Assyria is described as the rod of God's anger. Again the sovereignty and judgment of the Lord results in all things being for His purpose. Not determinism, but utility of the ultimate authority, towards His ends.

The proud of heart are an abomination to the Lord, even when they join forces against Him. I think of the armies Satan deceives into attacking Jesus and the camp of the saints at the end of the Millennial Kingdom, appealing to their pride. They unite for the battle of Gog and Magog, and are instantly destroyed, punished for their pride.

**Revelation 20:7-9**
*And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison, And shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog, and Magog, to gather them together to battle: the number of whom is as the sand of the sea. And they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them.*

As we have been instructed over and over again, fear of the Lord brings understanding and wisdom, wisdom brings mercy and love of truth, and these in practice purge iniquity and injustice from men.

By heeding the wisdom of the Lord, by seeking and walking in His paths, by acknowledging Him in all our ways, we please the Lord and rather than the destruction of the prideful and the visiting of evil, He will even make our enemies be at peace with us.

In **Genesis 26:28-29**, Isaac prospered and lived righteously, causing his chief enemy, King Abimelech, to come to him seeking a covenant of peace, acknowledging that God was with him.

This is most evident in the cycle of Judges.

**Judges 2:14-19**
*And the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of spoilers that spoiled them, and he sold them into the hands of their enemies round about, so that they could not any longer stand before their enemies. Whithersoever they went out, the hand of the Lord was against them for evil, as the Lord had said, and as the Lord had sworn unto them: and they were greatly distressed. Nevertheless the Lord raised up judges, which delivered them out of the hand of those that spoiled them.*

teachings.title: There is a way that seemeth right
teachings.summary: Man can rationalize any sin, but God's ways are higher than ours, so we must acknowledge Him and study His word to walk His paths, which alone lead to life.
teachings.text:
The chapter begins to wrap up with one of the most cited Proverbs.

*There is a way that seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.*

Man is able to rationalize any transgression, any trespass against others, every petty sin and idle thought. But man's ways are not God's.

**Isaiah 55:8-9**
*For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the Lord. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts*.

This is why God tells us to acknowledge Him in all our ways, that we may walk His paths. To study and gain knowledge, that we can know His thoughts. Because His way is life and ours death and there's no good end to the wicked.

Ungodly men dig up evil, and the words they say are destructive. They sow strife and with a froward mouth, cause friends to fight. The violent man tempts his neighbor, and entices them from God's way. The unrighteous devises perverse things to say, bringing evil to pass.

This is contrasted with the righteous elder, his gray head a crown of glory. Being slow to anger is the real might of a man. A man with in control of himself, will be able to rule others.

But either way, it is to God's purpose.

**Romans 8:28**
*And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.*

teachings.title: The Lord pondereth the hearts
teachings.summary: God ordains rulers and directs the king's heart, and He judges the spirit behind men's deeds, valuing mercy and judgment over sacrifice, so the sacrifice of the wicked is abomination.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 21** adds to the sayings of the king, first hand advice of Solomon to his heir, that God is the master and commander of the ship of state, as He sets the heart of the king to His own devices.

Just as the Lord said of Pharaoh;

**Romans 9:17**
*For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.*

And the government is on the shoulders of whom its given;

**Romans 13:1**
*Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.*

What a humbling saying for a young prince to hear. For good or ill, God's anointed is ordained to power in His will and to the Almighty Lord's purpose.

*Every way of a man is right in his own eyes: but the Lord pondereth the hearts.* The spirit behind what a man does, this is what God judges. The things we do in sin aren't only those things that no good led to, fornication, iniquity, theft, deceit, covetousness...those aren't the only ways we sin and fall short. Often we can do the right things for the wrong reasons. God knows our hearts.

That's why, especially for a prince, to do justice and judgment, with fairness and right spirit, means more to God than sacrifice. As Jesus says to the Pharisees;

**Matthew 9:13**
*But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance*.

This, quoting **Hosea 6:6**
*For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.*

This leads to a theme of the heart of the wicked. Their tendencies and traits.

The high look and proud heart of the wicked, their plans and schemes, this is sin. Diligence has a reward, haste leads to want.

Lying for wealth is a vanity, the wise king says, and it is passed back and forth between thieves, those that seek death and not life. There is no honor among thieves. Their robberies end in death. They are destroyed by their ways. They refuse judgment. Everything they seek to gain is motivated by greed and covetousness. Their way is froward and strange. But for the pure, those seeking to walk on God's path, their work is right.

The wicked desires evil. They do not love even their neighbors, violating even the second great command.

**Matthew 22:37-39**
*Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.*

In the end, God will overthrow the wicked for their wickedness. The wicked ignore the cries of the poor, and so God will not hear the wicked's cry.

Their love of pleasure results in poverty, that lack of impulse control. High time preference. This will ruin a man led by his own desires. A foolish man spends all he has.

Scorners are proud and haughty, their wrath comes from their pride. Overreacting to slights. Their pride insulted.

The lazy are their own destruction, the slothful kills themselves by their lack of labor. Their end is hunger. They shall always want.

The covetous, often the same foolish, lazy, proud and unjust fool, the robber, he who hates his neighbor, they are consumed by their greed all day long.

God promises the false witness will perish, and the wicked is set in their ways.

Tying this thread all back together to the beginning, we are given the understanding God judges hearts, the spirit of the man, and He values mercy and judgement over sacrifice, we see then the truth; *The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind?*

teachings.title: The limits of Solomon's wisdom
teachings.summary: Even Solomon's great wisdom could not find out all the ways of God, which are known only as God gives wisdom by His Spirit to those who seek Him.
teachings.text:
Finishing **Ecclesiastes 8,** Solomon again comes back to his observation that, with all things considered, the blessing to enjoy life's good things by our labors is a gift of God;

*Then I commended mirth, because a man hath no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry: for that shall abide with him of his labour the days of his life, which God giveth him under the sun.*

The Preacher has applied his heart, put in the effort to see all the business that is done in the earth, kept up at night by searching out all things. The wisdom of Solomon, applied in the tireless search of all he surveyed under the Sun, and his conclusion to the matter is that God has blessed those that work diligently in fear of the Lord, are blessed to enjoy the fruit of their labor.

But more, the King's search for understanding has led him to recognize that despite all his knowledge and wisdom, the ways of God are still far above him.

**1 Kings 4:29-30**
*And God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, and largeness of heart, even as the sand that is on the sea shore. And Solomon's wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east country, and all the wisdom of Egypt.*

He composed 3,000 proverbs and wrote 1,005 songs during his lifetime. In addition to his literary achievements, Solomon held an extensive knowledge of botany and zoology, speaking authoritatively about flora and fauna ranging from the massive cedar trees of Lebanon to the tiny hyssop growing out of the wall. His scientific observations also encompassed the animal kingdom, as he classified and described various beasts, birds, reptiles, and fish. And yet, though Man's wisdom, no matter how diligently he may apply his labors to seek it, man shall not be able to find out all the ways of God.

But we have access to His wisdom by other means. As a gift to those who diligently seek Him.

**1 Corinthians 2:12-14**
*Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God; that we might know the things that are freely given to us of God. Which things also we speak, not in the words which man's wisdom teacheth, but which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual. But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.*

Not by man's wisdom. But by His Spirit.

**Proverbs 2:6**
*For the LORD giveth wisdom: out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding.*

Solomon has reached the limit of his understanding, and now is leaning upon the Lord's.

teachings.title: Fear God and keep his commandments, the whole duty of man
